hints: Focus on the fact that you need to satisfy two separate tests at once, so check each compound for both features one by one.
Recall that a positive iodoform test needs a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group or a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group that can be oxidised to it.
Now look for a chiral carbon with four different groups attached, and see which iodoform-positive structure also has one.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

This is a test for methyl ketones and related structures. A yellow precipitate of tri-iodomethane forms if the molecule contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$.

Chemical rule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO-R} \xrightarrow{\text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH}} \text{CHI}_3 \text{(yellow ppt)}$$

**Recall optical isomerism**

A compound shows optical isomerism if it has a chiral centre. That is a carbon bonded to four different atoms or groups, with no plane of symmetry.

Check for:
$$\text{C}^* \text{ bonded to 4 different groups}$$

**Apply both tests to the options**

Option A, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(OH)CH}_3$, contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ so it gives a positive iodoform test. Its third carbon is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{COCH}_3$, so it is chiral and shows optical isomerism. It passes both tests, so it is the answer.

options.A: Correct. It has $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ so gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine. The $\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ carbon is attached to H, OH, CH3 and COCH3, four different groups, so it is chiral and shows optical isomerism.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ does give a positive iodoform test because of the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, but it has no chiral centre. Both $\text{CH}_2$ groups have two identical H atoms, so it cannot show optical isomerism.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CHO}$ is chiral because the middle carbon is bonded to H, CH3, CH2OH and CHO, so it shows optical isomerism. However it has neither $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ nor $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, and it is not ethanal, so the iodoform test is negative.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C(OH)CHO}$ has a central carbon bonded to two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so it is achiral and shows no optical isomerism. It also lacks $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so the iodoform test is negative.
